subj: How good is one-button PID autotune, really?
value: Build: relay autotune vs ZN/TL vs brute force on 4 plant loops; relay Ku off by 39% on fast loop, ZN unstable after drift
body:
Replacing PLCs with a controller built for AI made me curious how good today's one-button autotune actually is, so I simulated the classic relay test on four plant-style loops (flow, level, temperature, and one heavy on dead time) and compared it with brute-force tuning.

The relay test underestimated the ultimate gain by 39% on the fast flow loop. Ziegler-Nichols gains from it overshot 16 to 60% and went unstable on the level loop once the plant drifted 30%. The more conservative rule was safe but had 3 to 5 times the error on slow loops. Code and results: github.com/Venkat960407/relay-autotune
proof: I'm Venkat, a high school programmer in Redmond. I write the autonomous code for my VEX robotics team (C++, PID, odometry, IMU and rotation sensors), and we're ranked 12th in the world in Robot Skills.

subj: How much a crack-sealing robot drives with the nozzle off
value: Build: crack routing sim; flipping crack ends -40% dead travel, greedy+2-opt -77%; matters more as sealing gets faster
body:
Sealing cracks with a robot made me curious how much of the job is spent driving between cracks with the nozzle off, so I wrote a small routing study on random crack networks across a 30 by 20 m lot.

Just starting each crack from its nearer end cut that wasted travel by 40%, and a greedy route with 2-opt cut it by 77%. At today's sealing speed that saves about 4 minutes a lot, but if sealing gets 4x faster, a naive route would spend 42% of the job driving instead of 15%. Code and results: github.com/Venkat960407/crack-seal-route

subj: Content-defined chunking vs fixed blocks for robot updates
value: Build: delta deploy sim; CDC sends 1.6% vs 95% for fixed blocks; resume vs restart on flaky links
body:
Sending only the bytes that changed and resuming after drops made me want to see the numbers, so I wrote a small simulation of updating a 97 MB robot image over a flaky 2 Mbit/s link.

Fixed 64 KiB blocks barely helped: three tiny insertions shifted everything after them, so 95% of blocks looked new. Content-defined chunking resent only 1.6%. When the link dropped every 30 seconds, restarting from zero never finished, while resuming finished in under 8 minutes. Code and results: github.com/Venkat960407/delta-deploy-sim
